requirements.evidence: Config key at config/services.php:40 `'mention_id' => env('DISCORD_MENTION_ID')`; .env.example:10 `DISCORD_MENTION_ID=`. app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:43-53 accepts string|int, trims, matches `/^\d{17,20}$/` (trailing newline already removed by trim, so `$` cannot be fooled), otherwise null so no `<@`. Lines 30-36 reserve `mb_strlen($mention) + 1` and append "\n".$mention, so total stays <= 1800 and the mention survives; no-mention path (line 26-28) unchanged. send() signature, no-op, redaction and soft-fail untouched. Docs updated in docs/ops/devops.md and docs/ops/logging.md.

conventions.evidence: Matches sibling style (private helper with PHPDoc, config() reads, Pest tests in existing file); ops docs and .env.example updated as required. CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] not updated, which the 'Keep docs in sync' convention asks for.

security.evidence: Strict allow-list regex after trim (DiscordOpsAlert.php:51-53) rejects @everyone/@here and injected newlines/`>`; non-string/non-int values rejected at line 47. No change to redaction or webhook-URL handling.

simplicity.evidence: ~30 lines of production code: one helper `mentionId()` and a small branch in formatContent(); reuses the existing MaxContentLength constant and mb_substr truncation.

readability.evidence: Clear names (`$mention`, `$limit`, `mentionId()`), short explanatory comment at DiscordOpsAlert.php:32-33, PHPDoc on the helper; no dead code.

scope.evidence: Every touched file (.env.example, DiscordOpsAlert.php, config/services.php, two ops docs, the existing test file) serves the task; no unrelated edits.

issues.explanation: The conventions require a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] for changes like this one, and the diff has none.

No test that a valid id with surrounding whitespace is trimmed and accepted, and the embedded-newline cases use 3-digit ids, so they would be rejected by length alone and don't prove the newline/extra-character rejection.
`max(0, $limit)` guards against a case that can't happen, because the mention is at most 23 characters, well under 1800.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID config. It is validated as a 17–20 digit snowflake after trimming and appended as `<@id>` on its own line, with room reserved inside the 1800-character limit so truncation never drops it. The env var is documented in .env.example and both ops docs. The code is correct, minimal and well tested; the gaps are a missing CHANGELOG entry and a couple of test cases (valid id with whitespace, valid-length id with injected text), so I'd approve with nits.
